nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Climate action|Climate justice and equity|Recognition of climate debt_qna_000
nodes.label: Facts
nodes.question: How long have POPs and other PBTs been accumulating, according to the paragraph?
nodes.answer: According to the paragraph, POPs and other PBTs have been accumulating primarily over the last two centuries of industrial production and deposition.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Climate action|Climate justice and equity|Recognition of climate debt_qna_001
nodes.label: Facts
nodes.question: What was the gross value added of the environmental goods and services sector in the European Union in 2020?
nodes.answer: The gross value added of the environmental goods and services sector in the European Union exceeded 340 billion in 2020.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Climate action|Climate justice and equity|Recognition of climate debt_qna_002
nodes.question: What did Away and Wargame find regarding the relationship between poverty and ecological footprint in developing countries?
nodes.answer: Away and Wargame found a bidirectional causality relationship between poverty and ecological footprint in global panels and Africa, yet no causality was detected in developing countries in Asia, Latin America, and the Caribbean.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Climate action|Climate justice and equity|Recognition of climate debt_qna_003
nodes.label: Facts
nodes.question: How much do the environmental externalities from these sectors range annually?
nodes.answer: Environmental externalities from these sectors range between US$10.5 trillion and US$22.6 trillion annually.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Climate action|Climate justice and equity|Recognition of climate debt_qna_004
nodes.label: Taxonomy
nodes.question: What are the two main contributors to GHG emissions from AFOLU from 1990 to 2019?
nodes.answer: The two main contributors are land use, land use change, and forestry (LULUCF), and enteric CH4 emissions, which contributed 51% and 23%, respectively.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Climate action|Climate justice and equity|Recognition of climate debt_qna_005
nodes.label: Facts
nodes.question: Which region had the highest contribution of AFOLU to total emissions?
nodes.answer: Latin America and the Caribbean had the highest contribution of AFOLU to total emissions at 58%.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Climate action|Climate justice and equity|Recognition of climate debt_qna_006
nodes.label: Facts
nodes.question: What is the regional contribution of AFOLU to total emissions in Europe and North America?
nodes.answer: The contribution of AFOLU to total emissions in Europe and North America is 7%.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Climate action|Climate justice and equity|Recognition of climate debt_qna_007
nodes.label: Ethics and regulation
nodes.question: What progress has been observed in terms of agricultural emission removal among the largest AFOLU emitters?
nodes.answer: There has been no progress from the largest AFOLU emitters, which include Latin America, Southeast Asia, and Africa, despite some progress from fewer emitters.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Climate action|Climate justice and equity|Recognition of climate debt_qna_008
nodes.label: Facts
nodes.question: How does the financial situation in less developed countries affect environmental concerns?
nodes.answer: Financial constraints in less developed countries hinder the prioritization of environmental concerns, reflecting the challenge of balancing economic needs with sustainability.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Climate action|Climate justice and equity|Recognition of climate debt_qna_009
nodes.label: Strategy
nodes.question: What are some of the negative environmental and social impacts that have accumulated primarily in poorer countries due to global production networks?
nodes.answer: Poorer countries have faced negative environmental and social impacts such as child labour, exploitation of workers, deforestation, water and air pollution, and greenhouse gas emissions due to the expansion of global production networks.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Climate action|Climate justice and equity|Recognition of climate debt_qna_010
nodes.label: Strategy
nodes.question: How have richer countries achieved higher levels of environmental quality within their national boundaries?
nodes.answer: Richer countries have achieved higher levels of environmental quality within their national boundaries by geographically dissociating consumption from production and importing a large share of polluting goods from abroad, leading to international environmental impact shifting.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Climate action|Climate justice and equity|Recognition of climate debt_qna_011
nodes.label: Strategy
nodes.question: Why are Export Credit Agencies (ECAs) considered an important oversight in public financial institutions?
nodes.answer: ECAs are the largest source of bilateral public finance for fossil fuels, which locks recipient countries into fossil fuel energy systems.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Climate action|Climate justice and equity|Recognition of climate debt_qna_012
nodes.label: Ethics and regulation
nodes.question: What has been a significant oversight in the scholarly attention surrounding financial institutions and fossil fuels?
nodes.answer: The significant oversight has been the lack of focus on public bilateral financial institutions, especially Export Credit Agencies (ECAs).

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Climate action|Climate justice and equity|Recognition of climate debt_qna_013
nodes.label: Facts
nodes.question: What are Export Credit Agencies (ECAs) primarily known for in the context of public finance?
nodes.answer: ECAs are the largest source of bilateral public finance for fossil fuels.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Climate action|Climate justice and equity|Recognition of climate debt_qna_014
nodes.label: Facts
nodes.question: What is the title of the article that the correction pertains to?
nodes.answer: The title of the article is "Environmental taxation triggers persistent psychological resistance to climate policy."

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Climate action|Climate justice and equity|Recognition of climate debt_qna_015
nodes.label: Facts
nodes.question: What percentage of global methane emissions did Russia contribute in 2020?
nodes.answer: Russia contributed 20% of global methane emissions in 2020.

nodes.id: Subtopic:Environment|Climate action|Climate justice and equity|Recognition of climate debt_qna_016
nodes.label: Science and tech
nodes.question: What relationship did Udemba et al. (2020) analyze for China?
nodes.answer: They analyzed the relationship among pollutant emissions, energy consumption, Foreign Direct Investments (FDIs), and economic growth, showing a bidirectional causal flow between CO2 emissions and energy consumption.
